tools.name: validate_iban
tools.description: Validate an IBAN offline against the bundled SWIFT IBAN Registry snapshot: country, length, BBAN structure and MOD-97 check digits. Does not confirm the account exists.

tools.name: build_iban
tools.description: Build an IBAN from its BBAN fields and compute the MOD-97 check digits. Call without `fields` first to get the country's field template.

country_code.description: ISO 3166 alpha-2 country code, e.g. DE.

fields.description: Map of template field id to value, e.g. { bank: '37040044', account: '0532013000' }.

tools.name: check_bic
tools.description: ISO 9362 BIC syntax and ISO 3166 country-code checks. No bank directory is bundled. With `reference_path` (or the PAYMENT_INTELLIGENCE_REFERENCE_PATH setting), also looks the BIC up in the user's own BIC Directory, Payments Directory, BIC Plus or other provider export: name, location, current or expired, successor BIC, and service participation. A directory record does not prove reachability for a specific payment; never use it alone for routing or compliance decisions.

reference_path.description: Optional: the user's reference data, read locally. An unzipped SWIFTRef BIC Directory or Payments Directory folder, one of its files, a legacy SWIFTRef product file (BIC Plus, Bank Directory Plus, ...), or a CSV/TSV export from any provider.

as_of.description: Date for current or expired, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today.

tools.name: lookup_reference_data
tools.description: Look up BICs (BIC8 or BIC11), national clearing codes (sort codes, ABA, IFSC, CNAPS, ...) and LEIs in the user's own reference files, read locally: SWIFTRef BIC Directory and Payments Directory folders (IDENTIFIERS, including historical, PARTICIPANTS and RELATIONSHIPS files; layouts come from the STRUCTURES file), legacy SWIFTRef products (BIC Plus, BIC Directory 2018, Bank Directory Plus, IBAN Plus, SEPA routing, Reach Plus, gpi), or a CSV/TSV export from any provider or in-house system. Returns per identifier: directory records (name, town, country, current or expired, successor), national IDs linked to a BIC, service participation, and SSI relationship counts with masked accounts. Only matching records are returned. No reference data ships with the plugin.

ids.description: Identifiers to look up, up to 50 per call.

path.description: The reference data: a folder (for example an unzipped SWIFTRef download) or one file. Defaults to the PAYMENT_INTELLIGENCE_REFERENCE_PATH setting.

as_of.description: Date for current or expired, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today.

column_map.description: For a CSV/TSV whose headers are not recognised: map fields to header names, for example {"id": "Swift Code", "name": "Bank"}. Fields: id, idType, name, town, country, status, modification, start, stop, successor, linkedBic, service, participant, reach.

annotations.title: Look up identifiers in your reference data

tools.name: explain_payment_message
tools.description: Explain an ISO 20022 payment message. pacs.008, pacs.009 and camt.053 get a plain-language narrative; pacs.002, pacs.004, camt.052 and camt.054 get a structured field projection. Case messages (camt.056 cancellation request, camt.029 resolution, camt.110 investigation request, camt.111 investigation response, the older camt.026, camt.027, camt.028 and camt.087, and the Swift Tracker messages trck.003 alert and trck.005 case status) get the projection plus a `case` field: case id, investigation type, status, reason, the underlying payment's UETR and references, camt.111 answer details (booking confirmation, payment status, amendments, compensation, value date adjustment) and any MT 199 copy Swift embedded in a delivered camt.110, with what it leaves out. All get an operator summary and quick insights. Field projection for triage, not usage-guideline rule validation.

path.description: Path to a local XML file. Prefer this for real data so it never enters the chat.

tools.name: scrub_payment_message
tools.description: Replace names, IBANs, account ids, UETRs and references in a pacs/camt message with consistent pseudonyms. With `path` + `output_path`, writes the scrubbed copy to disk and returns only masked statistics, so the original data never enters the conversation. Never overwrites an existing file.

path.description: Path to a local XML file. Prefer this for real data so it never enters the chat.

output_path.description: Where to write the scrubbed XML. Must not exist yet and must differ from `path`.

tools.name: check_cbpr_readiness
tools.description: Local CBPR+ readiness hints: AppHdr/Document namespaces, schema-profile coverage, UETR, BIC and IBAN syntax. Readiness hints, not usage-rule validation.

path.description: Path to a local XML file. Prefer this for real data so it never enters the chat.

tools.name: analyze_payment_lifecycle
tools.description: Group a set of ACK/NACK, pacs and camt files by shared identifiers (UETR, EndToEndId, TxId) into threads with a timeline and warnings. Case messages (camt.026, camt.027, camt.028, camt.029, camt.056, camt.087, camt.110, camt.111) and Tracker messages (trck.003, trck.005) join the thread of the payment they quote; a camt.111 or trck.005 joins its camt.110 by EIR. Works only on the files given.

tools.name: validate_ssi_file
tools.description: Validate a standing settlement instruction (SSI) file: a SWIFTRef SSI Plus V3 extract or a CSV/TSV export. Checks BIC, ISO country, ISO 4217 currency and SSI asset-category formats, required fields, preferred flags, lifecycle dates, staleness, and conflicts (two preferred correspondents, overlapping active instructions). Rule ids match SSI Control Tower. Accounts are masked in the output.

ssi_path.description: Path to the local SSI file: SWIFTRef SSI Plus, a SWIFTRef Payments Directory RELATIONSHIPS file, or a CSV/TSV from any provider. Prefer this: the file never enters the chat.

ssi_content.description: The SSI file content, inline (small files only).

column_map.description: For an export whose headers are not recognised (any provider, for example LexisNexis or an in-house system): map SSI fields to header names, for example {"ownerBic": "Bank SWIFT", "accountHolderBic": "Nostro Agent", "currency": "Ccy"}. Fields: recordKey, ownerBic, ownerName, ownerCountry, ownerId, market, currency, assetCategory, accountHolderBic, accountHolderName, accountHolderCountry, account, preferredFlag, holderType, startDate, stopDate, status, lastConfirmed.

as_of.description: Date to judge active and stale instructions, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today.

tools.name: check_payment_against_ssi
tools.description: Check that a payment pays the beneficiary institution through the correspondent and account in the user's own SSI file. Reads the route from a pacs.008 (creditor agent, last intermediary, CdtrAgtAcct) or pacs.009 (creditor, creditor agent, CdtrAcct), or from explicit fields, then looks up owner BIC + currency + asset category and compares with the preferred SSI effective on the value date. Returns MATCH, ACCOUNT_MISMATCH, AGENT_MISMATCH, NOT_PREFERRED, AMBIGUOUS_SSI, NO_EFFECTIVE_SSI or NO_SSI per transaction. Accounts are masked.

ssi_path.description: Path to the user's SSI file: SWIFTRef SSI Plus V3, a SWIFTRef Payments Directory RELATIONSHIPS file, or a CSV/TSV from any provider.

ssi_content.description: The SSI file content, inline (small files only).

column_map.description: For an export whose headers are not recognised (any provider, for example LexisNexis or an in-house system): map SSI fields to header names, for example {"ownerBic": "Bank SWIFT", "accountHolderBic": "Nostro Agent", "currency": "Ccy"}. Fields: recordKey, ownerBic, ownerName, ownerCountry, ownerId, market, currency, assetCategory, accountHolderBic, accountHolderName, accountHolderCountry, account, preferredFlag, holderType, startDate, stopDate, status, lastConfirmed.

path.description: Path to a local XML file. Prefer this for real data so it never enters the chat.

owner_bic.description: Beneficiary institution BIC (the SSI owner). Overrides the message.

asset_category.description: SSI asset category such as COPA, CASH, FOEX, SECU. Overrides the default for the message type.

account_holder_bic.description: Correspondent (account-holding institution) BIC used by the payment. Overrides the message.

account.description: Account at the correspondent used by the payment. Overrides the message.

value_date.description: Value date, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to the message settlement date, else today.

tools.name: decode_reason_code
tools.description: Explain an ISO 20022 status or reason code such as RJCT, AC01 or MD07. Omit `code` to list the curated set.
